scenario.title: Busy walk-in, limited kit (challenging)
scenario.environment: Community walk-in clinic (no imaging on site)

learning_objectives.label: Introduce yourself, ask permission before examining and respond to the patient's pain
Examine the injured wrist systematically and compare with an uninjured area
Make a safe plan when imaging is not available on site
Keep communicating clearly with a worried companion and a noisy room

interventions.label: A helper arrives

line.speaker: Kim
line.text: Hi, I'm Kim, one of the nurses. Tell me what you need and I'll fetch it.

interpretation: Difficulty: Challenging. No coaching unless the instructor switches it on during the session.
Setting: Community walk-in clinic (no imaging on site), busy; noise level 60% at the end.

Investigation and management: 2 of 11 achievable points (the rubric maximum of 20 includes 'Requested appropriate imaging of the injured wrist', 'Interpreted the imaging result correctly', which could not be earned here).
Measurement and orthosis fitting: 0 of 16 achievable points (the rubric maximum of 20 includes 'Chose the size that matches the measurement', which could not be earned here).
This scenario is experimental, not clinician-reviewed.

feedback.summary: No conversation transcript was recorded, so history-taking and communication could not be assessed. You correctly considered a scaphoid injury. However, you did not ask about the mechanism of injury (how exactly the patient fell). Correct. A fall on an outstretched hand with anatomical snuffbox tenderness makes a scaphoid fracture the key diagnosis to suspect and exclude.

diagnostic_assessment.explanation: Correct. A fall on an outstretched hand with anatomical snuffbox tenderness makes a scaphoid fracture the key diagnosis to suspect and exclude.

next_steps: Complete the wrist examination: scaphoid tubercle tenderness and pain on axial thumb compression.
Request dedicated scaphoid-view radiographs; an initial X-ray can be normal.
If clinical suspicion remains despite normal X-rays: immobilise in a thumb spica splint and arrange repeat imaging or MRI.
Explain the plan and the risk of a missed scaphoid fracture (non-union, avascular necrosis) to the patient.
